oneLine: Solid, clean output across all five jobs with correct lemmas, clitics and corrections; the one real error is claiming 'echar de menos' is the standard Latin American way to say 'to miss', plus a handful of awkward notes and calques.

mistakes.item: echar (Voy a echar de menos a mi familia.)
mistakes.what: grammarNote says "'Echar de menos' is the standard Latin American way to say 'to miss' someone". That's backwards: in Latin America (Mexico especially) the everyday verb is 'extrañar', and 'echar de menos' sounds Peninsular. The note never mentions extrañar.

mistakes.item: vino (Pedimos una botella de vino tinto.)
mistakes.what: grammarNote says "the article 'una botella de' and the adjective 'tinto' show it is the noun". 'una botella de' is not an article, it's a noun phrase plus a preposition. Also 'wine (by the glass)' in otherMeanings is filler, not a different meaning.

mistakes.item: pena (Me da pena hablar en público.)
mistakes.what: meaningInContext is right (embarrassment), but the grammarNote and phraseMeaning hedge with "it makes me sad" and never say that in Mexico 'me da pena' mainly means 'I'm embarrassed/shy'. The learner is left unsure which meaning applies.

mistakes.item: quedé (Me quedé en casa porque llovía.)
mistakes.what: "In Latin America 'quedarse' is the usual verb for staying somewhere" adds a needless regional qualifier: 'quedarse' = 'to stay' everywhere.

mistakes.item: fui (Ayer fui al mercado con mi hermana.)
mistakes.what: otherMeanings lists 'to fit (clothing)' for ir. That's a stretch: 'te va bien' means 'it suits you'; 'to fit' is quedar.

mistakes.item: olvidó (Se me olvidó la llave en casa.)
mistakes.what: The 'se' clitic's refersTo is "the forgetting event (impersonal)", which is vague. The role ('accidental se') is right, though.

mistakes.item: Yo ___ en casa la semana pasada. (estuve)
mistakes.what: "I was at home last week" doesn't force the preterite: 'estaba' fits the English just as well, and the card allows only one try.

mistakes.item: Usted ___ en la oficina desde temprano. (ha estado)
mistakes.what: The English "You have been at the office since early" is awkward; 'since early this morning' would read better.
3 of the 10 cards are present tense (two of them the same 'está' + state/location pattern), and there's no conditional card ('estaría').
Both cards drill plural 'Cuáles' ('Which ones are on sale today?' / 'Which ones do we need for the recipe?'), and no card drills singular 'Cuál'.
The note "Cuánto is masculine singular here" is misleading: here it's the invariable adverb 'how much' and doesn't agree with any noun.

mistakes.item: ¿___ es el carro que vamos a llevar? (De quién)
mistakes.what: The Spanish is wordy and a bit unnatural for 'Whose car are we taking?'. '¿En el carro de quién nos vamos?' or '¿De quién es el carro?' would be more idiomatic.

mistakes.item: ___ mi paraguas en el carro. (He dejado)
mistakes.what: Mexican usage would say 'Dejé mi paraguas en el carro'. The present-perfect card leans Peninsular, even though the English forces it.
The English "Take an umbrella." doesn't force tú over usted ('Tome'). Also, 'Llévate un paraguas' is the more natural Mexican phrasing.

mistakes.item: Te ___. (voy a creer) / Ella ___ un regalo. (está recibiendo)
mistakes.what: Both English prompts are unnatural: 'I am going to believe you' and 'She is receiving a gift'. The answers are grammatical, though.
The notes list only the yo/tú/él forms ("llegué, llegaste, llegó", "pagué, pagaste, pagó") on cards whose answer is the nosotros form. They don't help.

mistakes.item: reply1: Suena como un día muy tranquilo en la playa.
mistakes.what: 'Suena como un día...' is an English calque; natural Spanish is 'Suena a un día muy tranquilo' or 'Qué día tan tranquilo'.

mistakes.item: reply2: El pozole es una gran elección, sobre todo con un buen caldo.
mistakes.what: Pozole is a soup, so "sobre todo con un buen caldo" is an odd, almost empty remark. 'Una gran elección' is also slightly calqued ('¡Qué rico!' would be more natural).

mistakes.item: Ayer comí en un restaurante y la comida estaba muy buena.
mistakes.what: 'estaba' is acceptable, but 'estuvo' is the more natural choice for a single meal eaten yesterday. A nit.

strengths: All the tricky lemmas are right: fui=ir, fue=ser, vino=noun, como=comer. Good disambiguation notes.
Clitic roles are correct for dáselo (se=IO replacing le, lo=DO) and se me olvidó (accidental se + IO experiencer).
'llevar + time + gerund' and 'me da pena' (embarrassment) are right in context.
Sentences: accurate translations, all idioms caught (sin embargo, darse cuenta, a lo mejor, hace…que, echar de menos), and nothing invented for 'El perro come pan'.
Drill: 10 clean cards with correct estar forms and Mexican-neutral Spanish, and no ser/estar traps.
Phrases: 10 cards per deck, every question opens with ¿, and they use Mexican vocabulary (carro, renta, pastel, autobús) with no Spain-only words.
Corrections are minimal and accurate: a la playa + comimos; la comida + buena + past tense; sentences 3 and 4 left untouched, with 'Yo' kept.
